A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FreCaS and contain readable main text, equations, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched across appendix renumbering. Increased image posterization in v2 affects visual quality but does not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on SD2.1, SDXL and SD3, spectral analysis, and guidance-weight and sampling-schedule ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds human evaluations, additional baseline comparisons, repeated-generation analysis and component ablations.

M1.justification: The cascaded sampling procedure, five-step resolution transition, FA-CFG and cross-attention reuse remain unchanged. Equations (1)-(6) and the method's operational description are retained; the new component ablations evaluate the existing method.

E1.justification: The LAION5B-based text-to-image task and evaluated resolution range remain unchanged. v1 already includes realistic and artistic images, complex scenes and varying aspect ratios. Additional prompt subsets, visual examples and human ratings extend evaluation without establishing a distinct generation task or dataset domain.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds evaluated comparisons with Pixart-Sigma, UltraPixel, SDXL+ESRGAN and SDXL+SUPIR, extending comparison to trained generators and super-resolution pipelines. The original comparator sets remain. ResMaster is newly discussed in related work but is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds FID alongside FIDb, three NR-IQA metrics, human preference and success-rate protocols, and component controls. New studies include 30 prompts with ten raters, separate five-rater evaluations, and 20 prompts with ten generations each. Appendix D specifies precision and sampler choices for new comparisons; existing benchmark settings in Table 2 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds sequential component ablations testing cascaded sampling, FA-CFG and attention reuse (Table 8), plus analyses of generation variability and human-rated success (Appendix D.2-D.3). These substantially extend v1's parameter and schedule sweeps, which remain in Figure 4 and renumbered Tables 9-10.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 explicitly evaluates generation variability using ten runs for each of 20 prompts. Table 5 reports average within-prompt standard deviations and standard deviations of prompt-level means for three quality metrics. This introduces a dedicated statistical evaluation; it does not establish repeated reruns of the original benchmark tables.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are retained, while substantial new results appear in Tables 1, 3-6 and 8 and additional figures. For example, SDXL ×4 gains a newly reported FID of 16.48 while retaining FIDb 12.63. New human evaluations report 60.7% preference for FreCaS in Figure 7, but only 27.2% successful judgments versus UltraPixel's 38.4% in Table 6.

T1.justification: The diffusion mathematics and Appendix A's SNR and timestep derivation are unchanged. Appendix D.2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of AoS and SoM through different aggregations of standard deviations and prompt-level means. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient training-free generation, frequency-aware guidance, layout preservation and applicability across diffusion models. Their headline speed and quality comparisons are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds substantive qualifications: FreCaS varies more across generations of the same prompt and has lower success than UltraPixel, despite favorable quality preferences. It also discusses sampler dependence and why downsampled global metrics can favor super-resolution methods. Appendix G adds interpretations of individual component contributions.

D1.justification: v2 documents precision and sampler choices for added comparisons, participant selection and presentation procedures for user studies, and an access link described as providing uncompressed images. The original code link, FreCaS hyperparameters in Table 2 and A100 timing setup are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused references for trained generators, super-resolution baselines and NR-IQA metrics. Section 2.2 extends its comparison with DemoFusion to ResMaster and clarifies the distinction between complete diffusion at each resolution and FreCaS's continuous process. The central training-free research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged. Local revisions update related-work wording, evaluation descriptions, affiliations and publication headers. New appendix sections move former Appendices C-E to E-G and require updated cross-references, without extensively rewriting the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 1 with an FID column and adds substantial displays for human studies, new comparisons, variability and component ablations. Existing appendix displays are relocated and renumbered. Several retained image grids also lose considerable tonal and texture fidelity, notably v1 Figure 7 versus v2 Figure 9, weakening fine-detail inspection.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation that v1 lacked: direct human assessments, comparisons with trained and super-resolution alternatives, repeated-generation analysis and component ablations. It also exposes meaningful reliability limitations instead of reporting only favorable aggregate results. These gains outweigh the visibly poorer fidelity of several image grids, although that deterioration materially weakens the supplied PDF's evidence about fine visual details.
